title: Z Group — Bilingual Real Estate Corporate Website & CMS
summary: A bilingual (EN/AR) corporate website and admin content management system that lets a real estate development company autonomously manage projects, marketing pages, and leads.
description: Z Group is a full digital ecosystem for a premier real estate developer, combining a public marketing site with a private admin console. Visitors can browse active, upcoming, and previous projects with galleries, floor plans, amenities, location maps, and construction timelines; submit project inquiries, register interest on landing pages, and apply for careers. The authenticated admin dashboard gives the marketing team complete control over project listings, a modular drag-and-drop landing page builder, every site section and SEO setting, and all form submissions — removing the need for developer intervention for every content change.
highlights: Engineered a modular, typed section-based landing page builder (hero, stats, content, features, gallery, CTA) with reorder/enable/disable controls persisted as a typed union of MongoDB models.

Built a custom weighted SEO scoring engine (SeoAnalyzer) with 8 rule checkers (title, description, headings, keyword density, images, URL, content structure, readability) that scores and recommends fixes for both English and Arabic content.

Designed a bilingual-first data model with localized {en, ar} strings throughout, an RTL-aware frontend, and an aggregated analytics dashboard powered by MongoDB aggregation pipelines across 11 collections.
features: Bilingual public site (English/Arabic) with next-intl i18n, locale routing, and RTL support
Project portfolio with gallery images/videos, floor plans, amenities, nearby places, partner logos, and location maps
Under-construction project pages with construction progress timelines and image sets
Previous projects showcase with reorderable item management
Admin dashboard with portfolio stats, donut/bar charts, recent activity, and quick actions
Drag-and-drop landing page builder with modular content sections and draft/publish workflow
Site settings manager for home, about, milestones, achievement video, footer, and page SEO
Integrated real-time SEO analyzer with weighted scores and actionable recommendations
Form submission management for project inquiries, landing page interest, careers (CV upload), and about-us contacts
JWT-based admin authentication with bcrypt password hashing and admin-only RBAC middleware
challenges: Modeling a flexible yet type-safe section-based page system: a discriminated union of section models (Hero, Stats, Content, Features, Gallery, CTA) with per-section props, ordering, and enabled flags on both the API and the client renderer.

Implementing a locale-aware weighted SEO analysis engine that evaluates content quality independently for English and Arabic, computing a live score from passed/total rule weights and surfacing severity-ranked issues in the editor.

Orchestrating a single aggregated dashboard endpoint that concurrently counts, trends, and snapshots data across 11 MongoDB collections using Promise.all and aggregation pipelines while keeping consistent response shapes for the charting UI.
architecture: Next.js 16 App Router frontend with next-intl locale routing (en/ar) and RTL support, consuming an Express 5 REST API backed by MongoDB (native driver) for content with PostgreSQL via pg for relational data. JWT access tokens in httpOnly cookies with bcrypt hashing protect admin routes, Multer handles media/CV uploads served as static files, and Zod validates all payloads.

title: Shopify–Shippo Bridge
summary: A Shopify App that connects merchants' stores to the Shippo shipping API for automated order fulfillment, label purchasing, and shipment tracking.
description: A full-stack Shopify App that bridges Shopify stores to the Shippo shipping platform. Merchants install the app via OAuth, and incoming Shopify orders are automatically ingested through webhooks. From there, the app handles the full fulfillment workflow: creating and validating addresses in Shippo, comparing shipping rates, purchasing labels, requesting carrier pickups, and syncing fulfillment status back to Shopify. A configurable shipping rules engine lets merchants automate rate selection based on order value, weight, or delivery window.
highlights: Shopify OAuth integration with JWT session management, httpOnly cookie auth, and automatic token refresh with request queuing
Automated order ingestion via Shopify webhooks that creates validated Shippo addresses and maps line items in a single pass
Bulk carrier pickup processing using RabbitMQ for background job queues with real-time progress streaming over SSE via Redis pub/sub
Shipping rules engine that evaluates prioritized conditions (order value, weight, always-apply) to auto-select the cheapest qualifying rate within a delivery window
features: Shopify OAuth app installation with scoped access and webhook registration
Automatic order ingestion from Shopify orders/create webhook with Shippo address validation
Shipment creation with Shippo rate comparison and label purchasing
Configurable shipping rules with prioritized conditions, max delivery days, and drag-to-reorder
Bulk pickup requests with background processing and live SSE progress updates
Address management with Shippo validation and local storage
Shipment tracking with status updates synced back to Shopify fulfillments
Dark/light theme with system preference detection
challenges: Coordinating asynchronous bulk pickup jobs across RabbitMQ, Redis pub/sub, and SSE streaming while handling partial failures gracefully
Mapping and syncing shipment tracking statuses between Shippo and Shopify's fulfillment system, including creating fulfillments and fulfillment events on demand
Designing the Shopify OAuth lifecycle with short-lived access tokens, long-lived refresh tokens, and a frontend interceptor that queues and retries requests on 401
architecture: React SPA frontend communicating with an Express backend, backed by MongoDB for persistence, Redis for pub/sub (SSE streaming), and RabbitMQ for background job processing. Integrates with Shopify's REST/GraphQL APIs and Shippo's REST API for shipping operations.

title: E-Commerce
summary: A full-stack e-commerce platform for browsing products, managing shopping carts, processing secure payments, and tracking orders.
description: A production-oriented e-commerce application built with a modular TypeScript backend and a modern Next.js frontend. The platform provides product discovery, category browsing, product variants and SKUs, shopping cart management, address management, checkout, Stripe payments, order tracking, email verification, and secure authentication. The backend follows a domain-based architecture with dedicated modules for authentication, products, categories, carts, orders, addresses, payments, and webhooks.
highlights: Complete product catalog with categories, product details, product attributes, SKUs, inventory quantities, pricing, cover images, and image galleries.
Secure authentication system with registration, login, password hashing, JWT access tokens, refresh tokens, HTTP-only cookies, and email verification.
Shopping cart functionality linked to authenticated users and product SKUs.
Multi-step checkout flow with saved addresses, shipping details, order review, and payment processing.
Stripe Payment Element integration for secure online payments.
Stripe webhook handling for synchronizing payment and order statuses.
Order creation from cart items with calculated subtotals and order items.
Product image upload and processing using Multer, Sharp, and S3-compatible object storage.
Redis-based refresh token storage and email verification token management.
Responsive storefront with home, shop, product details, cart, checkout, authentication, and order history pages.
Reusable frontend state and data-fetching layers using Redux Toolkit and SWR.
PostgreSQL relational data model with users, categories, products, SKUs, carts, orders, addresses, and payments.
features: User registration and login
Email verification flow
JWT-based authentication
Refresh token rotation and validation
Product catalog browsing
Category filtering
Product search and filtering interface
Product variants and SKU selection
Product image galleries
Add-to-cart functionality
Cart item quantity management
Saved shipping addresses
Multi-step checkout
Stripe payment processing
Payment webhook verification
Order creation and order history
Order details retrieval
Product and SKU image uploads
Image optimization with Sharp
Cloud object storage integration
Redis caching and token storage
Transactional email delivery
Responsive user interface
Centralized API error handling
Modular backend services and repositories
challenges: Designing a consistent data model for products, product variants, SKUs, carts, orders, order items, and payments.
Keeping cart, order, and payment states synchronized across the checkout process.
Implementing secure authentication using short-lived access tokens, refresh tokens, HTTP-only cookies, Redis storage, and email verification.
Handling Stripe webhook requests using the raw request body for reliable signature verification.
Managing product covers, galleries, and SKU images through multipart uploads and S3-compatible object storage.
Supporting product variants while preserving accurate pricing, quantities, and inventory information.
Building a responsive checkout experience with saved addresses and Stripe's Payment Element.
Separating domain responsibilities through controllers, services, repositories, routes, and typed data transfer objects.
Handling asynchronous operations such as email delivery, payment processing, and background payment workers.
Providing consistent error handling across the API and frontend.
architecture: The application uses a full-stack architecture with a Next.js and React frontend communicating with a modular Express API through REST endpoints under /api. The backend is organized by business domains, including authentication, products, categories, carts, orders, addresses, payments, and webhooks. Each domain generally follows a controller-service-repository pattern with dedicated TypeScript types. PostgreSQL stores the core relational data, Redis manages refresh tokens and temporary verification tokens, Stripe handles payment intents and payment confirmation, RabbitMQ supports background payment processing, Resend handles transactional emails, and S3-compatible storage is used for product media. The frontend uses feature-based organization, Redux Toolkit for client state, SWR for server data fetching, and Stripe Elements for secure payment collection.

title: Markteer
summary: A marketing agency website and CMS for showcasing services, projects, career opportunities, and managing client inquiries.
description: A full-stack website and content management system built for a digital marketing agency. The public website showcases the agency's services and portfolio, while visitors can explore projects, submit inquiries, apply for jobs, and subscribe to the newsletter. An admin dashboard gives the team control over website content, projects, services, jobs, offices, messages, and media.
highlights: Full-stack CMS with a protected admin dashboard for managing the agency's website content and media.
Rich project showcase with service-based filtering, featured projects, related projects, galleries, and detailed project pages.
Centralized content management for services, projects, jobs, offices, newsletters, and client inquiries using PostgreSQL and Prisma.
Contact and career workflows that store submissions and trigger email notifications through external email services.
Performance-focused Next.js implementation using server-side data fetching, lazy loading, and optimized image handling.
features: Service pages with detailed content and related portfolio projects.
Portfolio browsing with service filters, search, featured projects, and project detail pages.
Rich project pages with galleries, client information, and formatted content.
Career section with office and job listings and online applications.
Contact form for client inquiries with admin message management.
Newsletter subscription and promotional spotlight content.
Protected admin CMS for managing services, projects, jobs, offices, newsletters, messages, and media.
challenges: Designing a flexible CMS structure that supports different types of agency content while keeping the public website and admin dashboard consistent.
Managing media-heavy project content, including image uploads, ordering, galleries, and project relationships.
Implementing protected admin routes and APIs while keeping the public website accessible without authentication.
Handling contact submissions reliably by storing messages independently from external email delivery.
architecture: A Next.js full-stack application using PostgreSQL and Prisma for data persistence. Public pages and admin interfaces share the same application, with protected admin routes secured through JWT authentication and middleware. API route handlers manage content, submissions, and uploads, while external email services handle notifications and communication workflows.
